text: I'll start with the StatefulSet and its PVC.

arguments.root_cause_statement: The StatefulSet analytics/metrics-db declares a volumeClaimTemplate "data" with storageClassName "fast-ssd", but the only StorageClass in this cluster is "standard" (provisioner rancher.io/local-path, marked default). The PVC the StatefulSet created for its pod, data-metrics-db-0, therefore inherits storageClassName "fast-ssd" and the persistentvolume-controller rejects it with ProvisioningFailed: storageclass.storage.k8s.io "fast-ssd" not found. With the claim stuck Pending and unbound, the scheduler cannot place metrics-db-0 (FailedScheduling: pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims), so the pod stays Pending, the StatefulSet stays 0/1 Ready, and service/metrics-db has zero endpoint addresses, which is why the analytics dashboards are empty. Fixing it means correcting the storage class name in the StatefulSet's volumeClaimTemplate to "standard"; because volumeClaimTemplates and existing PVC storageClassName are immutable, the StatefulSet must be recreated (e.g. kubectl delete sts metrics-db --cascade=orphan) and the stale Pending PVC data-metrics-db-0 deleted so it is recreated against "standard".
arguments.mechanism: StatefulSet analytics/metrics-db sets .spec.volumeClaimTemplates[0].spec.storageClassName to "fast-ssd", a StorageClass that does not exist in this cluster (the only one is "standard"), so the generated claim data-metrics-db-0 is rejected by the persistentvolume-controller with ProvisioningFailed "storageclass.storage.k8s.io \"fast-ssd\" not found" and stays unbound, leaving pod metrics-db-0 unschedulable with unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims.

evidence.claim: The paged StatefulSet has no ready replica and its only pod is unscheduled.
Service metrics-db has no endpoint addresses, so dashboards get nothing.
The StatefulSet's volumeClaimTemplate asks for StorageClass fast-ssd.
evidence.quote:
Volume Claims:
  Name:          data
  StorageClass:  fast-ssd

evidence.claim: The claim generated from that template carries storageClassName fast-ssd.
Provisioning of the claim fails because that StorageClass does not exist.
evidence.quote: Warning  ProvisioningFailed  1s (x2 over 1s)  persistentvolume-controller  storageclass.storage.k8s.io "fast-ssd" not found

evidence.claim: The only StorageClass present in the cluster is standard, the default.
The unbound claim is what keeps the pod from being scheduled.
evidence.quote: Warning  FailedScheduling  0s    default-scheduler  0/1 nodes are available: pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims. not found

ruled_out.alternative: The node lacked capacity or carried a taint that blocked scheduling.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The single node is Ready with full allocatable CPU, memory and 110 pod slots and no taints listed; scheduling failed on the volume, not on capacity.
ruled_out.quote:
node/incident-lab-control-plane cpu=6/6 memory=12220316Ki/12220316Ki pods=110 (capacity/allocatable)
  condition Ready=True

ruled_out.alternative: The Service selector does not match the pod labels, so endpoints are empty for a labeling reason.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The Service selector app=metrics-db exactly matches the pod's labels; the pod simply never reaches Running/Ready because it is Pending and unscheduled.

ruled_out.alternative: The container image or command is broken (crash loop / bad image).
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pod never started a container at all: it has no node and only a PodScheduled=False condition, so no image pull or command execution was ever attempted.
